summary: Robotics software engineer with 8 years in robotics across research and industry, starting with award-winning undergraduate research in autonomous ground robots. I take mapping, perception and navigation from algorithm design to deployment on real robots. I built and flew a custom autonomous drone with onboard perception, and led a three-engineer team that deployed more than 30 commercial robots.

experience.role: Doctoral researcher, robotics and computer vision
experience.note: PhD project: autonomous real-time UAV mapping with spatial perception for indoor applications. Supervised by George Vosselman and Francesco Nex.
bullets: Developed C++ software for monocular visual-inertial SLAM and 3D scene-graph mapping in ROS 2 (Mono-Hydra++). Sparse predicted-depth factors in the factor graph cut trajectory error by 61% on ScanNet against monocular GO-SLAM while holding 25 to 30 Hz.

Designed the multi-task deep learning architecture for joint depth estimation and semantic segmentation (M2H, M2H-MX). M2H appeared at IEEE/RSJ IROS 2025; M2H-MX, accepted at the IEEE ICRA 2026 SRRA Workshop, improves NYUDv2 mIoU by 6.6% and depth RMSE by 9.4% over the best tested baseline.
Built a custom autonomous drone and deployed onboard perception on its Jetson Orin NX 16GB, exported through ONNX and optimised with TensorRT FP16, processing images at 25.5 frames per second.

Developed ATLAS, an autonomous exploration algorithm on top of that mapping system: a compact belief graph of places and open ends keeps goal selection real time, trained in Isaac Sim from planner demonstrations and deep reinforcement learning, integrated with Mono-Hydra++ over ROS 2 and deployed on the drone.
Prepared and taught practical exercises for two master's courses in robot perception and autonomy, and supervised three master's thesis students.

loop.title: Perception and scene graph
loop.note: M2H-MX predicts metric depth and semantics in a single pass, and Mono-Hydra++ turns them into a hierarchical 3D scene graph. The same stack, run across different environments.

loop.title: Robustness on device
loop.note: The VIO running on a Jetson Orin with a ZED X One, holding pose down the stairs and back up. This is the robustness test for the algorithm.

loop.title: The drone
loop.note: The quadrotor built to deploy this stack, carrying and computing all of it onboard.

loop.title: Exploration
loop.note: Still at simulation level, in NVIDIA Isaac Sim and the lab: the map it built decides where to look next. Deployment on the drone comes next.

experience.role: Senior robotics software engineer and project lead
experience.note: Joined as the founding robotics engineer and was promoted within 10 months to lead a three-engineer team.
bullets: Developed navigation software and led deployments of more than 30 robots for more than 10 enterprise clients, including a six-month run at Expo 2020 Dubai, resolving sensor and software integration issues on site.

Integrated ROS and GMapping navigation, LiDAR and 3D obstacle sensing with vendor robot SDKs and voice assistance for autonomous visitor guidance, recovering localisation failures on site in changing crowd conditions.
Fine-tuned a YOLOv5 face detector for grayscale thermal imagery and deployed it on an Intel NUC with a FLIR camera for contactless temperature screening, running live across enterprise sites.
